newsitem.title: USA: Exide European unit to buy companies. [CORRECTED 19:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Exide European unit to buy companies. [CORRECTED 19:27 GMT]

text.p: Exide Corp, which makes automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries, said Wednesday its Exide Holding Europe unit intends to buy all the shares of three European battery firms.
The three companies, DETA Akkumulatoranwark GmbH, MAREG Accumulatoren GmbH and FRIWO SILBERKRAFT, are based in Germany and are currently owned by CEAG AG.
The companies, with subsidiaries in the United Kingdom, Spain and Portugal, make automotive, industrial and specialty batteries.
The purchase is subject to certain approvals by the German Federal Cartel Office as well as the approval of CEAG AG's shareholders, Exide said. Terms were not disclosed.

"This purchase concludes our acquisition strategy and strengthens our presence in Europe," Arthur Hawkins, chairman of Exide Corp, said in a statement. "It also complements our existing European operations and presents us further opportunities for rationalization and profit growth" (company corrects statement). ((Reuters Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
